outcome: No proof, disproof, or any mathematical progress toward the infinitude of Pierpont primes has been found since 26 January 2024; the conjecture remains open and undisturbed.
summary: Pierpont primes are primes of the form 2^u·3^v + 1. Andrew Gleason's conjecture that there are infinitely many of them (per the count heuristic ~9n up to 10^n) remains unproven as of today, and every source checked (the current Wikipedia article on Pierpont primes, the Prime Pages glossary entry, and OEIS A005109) still states or implies this is an open conjecture with no resolution. The only concrete numerical fact in this area — the largest known Pierpont prime, 81 × 2^20498148 + 1 (6,170,560 digits), verified in June 2023 — predates the 26 January 2024 window and is in any case a record/search result rather than a statement bearing on infinitude (per §3.1, existence/infinitude questions move only when answered, not when the search frontier is extended). No newer record was found in searches of PrimeGrid-related coverage or general web search, and no arXiv paper, blog post, or announcement since January 2024 was found addressing the infinitude question directly — a search for arXiv papers with 'Pierpont primes' in the 2024-2025 window returned only unrelated number-theory papers (e.g. on primes p where p-1 is a sum of two squares) that merely appeared due to keyword overlap in sieve-theory search results. The one 2024-dated edit found on OEIS A005109 (a September 2024 formula restatement by Amiram Eldar) is a notational addition, not new mathematics, and does not bear on the conjecture. No AI system was found anywhere near this problem. This is a clean 'nothing happened' case, matching the triage's own conclusion.
competing_reading: None found. There is no plausible alternative classification here — no source suggests any movement, partial result, or bound relevant to the infinitude question in the window, and no case-restriction (e.g. a proof for a fixed v or u) was found either.
what_would_settle_it: A proof or disproof of Gleason's conjecture on Pierpont prime infinitude, or a partial result restricting the question to a sub-case (e.g. a density/lower-bound result specifically for numbers of the form 2^u·3^v+1) published as a preprint, journal article, or expert-digested announcement after 26 January 2024, would change this record.
